collins.hedgehog: Become the best, most convenient drugstores, with high profit per customer visit: dense clusters of stores on the best corners so a customer is never far from one, plus services such as convenient pharmacy. Economic denominator: profit per customer visit (not per store).
collins.stop_doing: Exit food service entirely (the restaurants and lunch counters the company had run for decades), which Cork Walgreen committed to doing within five years; also exit the discount department stores.
collins.leader_type: Level 5 (Charles 'Cork' Walgreen III: modest family heir, set the hedgehog and drove the exit from restaurants against family tradition)
brutal_facts: net margin is very low and earnings have stalled while sales doubled
capital is spread across restaurants and discount stores
discount stores are losing money in the recession

later_history: 1975-1990 cumulative stock returns about 7.34x the general market (per Collins). Liquidated the Globe discount stores in 1976. Cut in-store restaurants from 231 (1979) to 119 (1984) and sold its Wag's restaurants to Marriott in 1988. Linked all stores by satellite pharmacy network in the 1980s; opened its 1,000th store in 1984 and 4,000th in 2003, with freestanding stores and drive-through pharmacies. Later decline: merged into Walgreens Boots Alliance (2014); the Theranos blood-testing partnership collapsed (2016); paid billions in opioid-related settlements (about $5.7B nationally in 2022); profits and share price fell sharply in the 2020s with mass store closures; taken private by Sycamore Partners in 2025.
notes: Track A matched pair with A20 (Eckerd). Walgreen's fiscal 1974 annual report (archive.org) supplies the dossier's financial table.
